anomalies.observed: T5 is an AON6407 P-channel MOSFET, but the netlist connects its source pin (T5.2) to the fused input node /+24V_F and its drain pin (T5.3) to the board +24V rail. The gate network (R10 and D1) is referenced to /+24V_F.
anomalies.expected: For a P-channel MOSFET used as reverse-polarity protection, the source should be on the protected load side (+24V) and the drain on the input side (/+24V_F), so the body diode points from input to output and blocks reverse polarity/backfeed. The source/drain connection in T5 is reversed for this standard topology.

evidence.quote: README states the PCB includes "reverse polarity protection, TVS diodes, proper isolation"

anomalies.impact: With correct polarity the rail may still power up, but the protection function is compromised: on reversed input the P-MOSFET body diode can conduct, and when the input is removed the +24V rail capacitors can backfeed through the body diode into the input connector.

parsed.summary: The design files otherwise match the specification, but the AON6407 reverse-polarity MOSFET T5 appears to have its source and drain connected opposite the standard P-channel reverse-polarity topology, making the input protection ineffective under reverse or removed-input conditions.
